what: The Morse Code Translator turns text into Morse code and Morse code back into text, live as you type. You can also hear the code as beeps, watch it flash as a light, feel it as vibration on many phones, or download it as a sound file.

It is useful for students and hobbyists learning Morse, amateur radio operators practising, scouts and teachers, puzzle and escape-room makers, and anyone curious about the code. Speed, tone, volume and letter spacing can be adjusted.
Everything runs in your browser, with no sign-up.
uses: Type letters and listen to them at a slow speed with extra spacing.
Paste dots and dashes from a puzzle, film or game to read them as text.
Use Full-screen flash to turn your phone or computer screen into a signal lamp.
Create Morse messages and sound files for treasure hunts and escape rooms.
Download WAV files at your target speed to practise copying code.
tutorial: Type in the Text box. The Morse code appears on the right, with letters separated by spaces and words by a slash.
Type or paste dots and dashes in the Morse code box. Dots like • and dashes like − are understood too. Unknown codes show as #.
Move Speed (5 to 40 words per minute), Tone (300 to 1200 Hz) and Volume.
Press Play. The lamp lights up for each signal and shows the letter being sent. Tick or untick Sound, Flash light and Vibrate.
Press Full-screen flash to make the whole screen blink. Tap anywhere or press Esc to stop.
Download sound (.wav) saves the audio (up to 10 minutes). Copy text and Copy Morse copy either side.
features: Text to Morse and Morse to text, live.
Hear, see and feel the code.
Speed in WPM with standard timing, plus Farnsworth spacing for learners.
Supports Ä, É, Ñ, Ö, Ü and more, plus punctuation.
Small, clean audio files you can share or practise with.
Even very long texts start playing instantly.

example.title: Worked example: SOS
example.text: Type SOS in the Text box. The Morse box shows ... --- ... (three dots, three dashes, three dots). Press Play at 18 WPM: you hear three short beeps, three long beeps and three short beeps, about 2 seconds in total, while the lamp flashes the same pattern. Press Download sound (.wav) to save it.

tips: Learn by sound, not by counting dots: listen to whole letters at 15 to 20 WPM with extra spacing on.
Use a slash or three spaces between words when typing Morse, or words will run together.
On a phone, turn the screen brightness up before using Full-screen flash.
Vibration works on most Android phones; iPhones do not allow websites to vibrate.
If you get # in the text, check that each letter is separated by a single space.
problems: Make sure Sound is ticked, the volume slider is up and your device is not muted.
Morse letters must be separated by spaces. Without spaces, .-.. could be read as one letter (L) instead of A and I.
They have no standard Morse code, such as emoji or Chinese characters. The message lists them.
The download says it is too long
Sound files are limited to 10 minutes. Raise the speed or split the text.
